claims.text: Fully recrystallizing the ductile phase while preserving the hard phase will simultaneously increase strength and ductility relative to an as-cast lamellar EHEA.
The initial material is an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with a fine lamellar FCC+B2 microstructure.
In the initial microstructure, the FCC phase is soft and ductile, whereas the B2 phase is hard.
A controlled thermal or thermomechanical treatment can selectively recrystallize the ductile FCC phase while retaining the reinforcing B2 phase.
There is a temperature-time window that allows full FCC recrystallization while restricting B2 recrystallization and grain growth.
Short-term annealing after deformation is a suitable route for achieving phase-selective recrystallization.
The treatment produces a fully recrystallized soft phase embedded in a hard-phase skeleton.
The resulting FCC matrix is refined and the B2 skeleton remains continuous.
Selective recrystallization reduces pre-existing strain incompatibilities and eliminates weak boundaries.
The phase-selectively recrystallized microstructure activates or releases the strain-hardening capacity of the duplex phases.
The retained B2 phase continues to provide high load-bearing capacity.
The combined response of the recrystallized FCC phase and retained B2 phase delays crack initiation and propagation at phase boundaries.
The treated alloy will have higher yield strength and ultimate tensile strength than the untreated as-cast alloy.
The treated alloy will have higher uniform elongation than the untreated as-cast alloy.
A phase-selectively recrystallized EHEA can achieve approximately 2 GPa true stress and approximately 35% uniform elongation.
The as-cast fine lamellar FCC+B2 baseline exhibits a strength-ductility trade-off.
The intervention requires a duplex alloy with distinguishable soft and hard phases and a processing window that selectively recrystallizes the soft phase.
The magnitude of the improvement depends on alloy composition and the temperature-time profile, and excessive treatment may cause coarsening or interfacial degradation.
